title: Serving Runtime: Architecture, Kernel Scheduling, Profiling & Runbooks
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Consolidated reference for the Redwood serving runtime: high-level architecture, kernel scheduling decisions, profiling playbooks, benchmarking suite, release notes, known issues, operational runbooks, and links to the team wiki.
overview: This document is the canonical entry point for engineers and SREs who operate or develop the Redwood serving runtime. It combines architecture diagrams and rationale, kernel scheduling and placement rules, profiling and benchmarking procedures, recent release notes that impact runtime behavior, a curated list of known issues and mitigations, and runbooks for common incidents. The goal is to reduce time-to-resolution for incidents and to provide reproducible performance testing for model onboarding and regression detection.
runtime_components:
High-level components:

- Frontdoor (API Gateway): request ingress, auth, rate limiting, initial overload protection.
- Router: smart routing policy engine (latency/cost/region/customer-tier) that maps requests to serving pools.
- Pool Manager: manages GPU pools (hosted/dedicated/private), scaling, and allocation.
- Worker Runtime: GPU-optimized inference engine running on each node. Responsibilities: model loading, KV cache, attention kernels, quantized execution paths.
- Cache Service: prefix and KV cache with TTL-based eviction and per-customer isolation.
- Telemetry & Tracing: per-request traces (OpenTelemetry), token-level metrics, and ingestion into observability pipeline.
- Orchestration / Control Plane: model versioning, rollouts, canaries, and automatic fallback policies.

Cross-cutting concerns: kernel selection, batching, memory accounting, graceful degradation, and security (KMS/HSM integrations).
kernel_scheduling:
Goals and constraints:

- Goals: minimize 99th-percentile latency, maximize GPU utilization, and limit OOMs during dynamic batching.
- Constraints: mixed model architectures (decoder-only / encoder-decoder), variable sequence lengths, multi-tenant isolation, and quantization differences.

Scheduling strategy summary:

1) Topology-aware placement: schedule heavy KV-cache / large-context models onto nodes with NVLink topology and larger HBM.
2) Kernel selection: at model load time the runtime probes available kernels (cuBLAS, CUTLASS custom, Triton kernels) for target shapes and selects the fastest stable kernel for the common sequence length quantiles.
3) Continuous profiling feedback: runtime periodically benchmarks hot kernels for the current hardware/driver stack and auto-updates the kernel priority list with a safe rollback window.
4) Batch-aware scheduling: requests are admitted into a batching queue with dynamic max_batch_size that adapts by observed latency and SLO headroom.

Deterministic fallback rules:

- If kernel probe fails or a new kernel increases p99 beyond configured delta (default +15%), revert to last-known-good kernel and raise an alert.
- If node memory pressure > 85%, evict non-critical cached items and refuse new large-context requests when necessary.
- If continuous batching increases observed median latency by > 20ms or p99 by > 10%, reduce max_batch_size by 25% and notify on-call.

Configuration knobs (examples):

- kernel_probe_interval: "3600s"
- kernel_probe_shapes: "[8x512, 16x1024, 32x2048]"
- max_node_memory_util_pct: "85"
- batch_admission_policy: "adaptive"
- batch_latency_headroom_ms: "20"
profiling_playbook:
Purpose: produce reproducible performance profiles for models and serving configurations used by runtime engineers, SRE, and model onboarding teams.

When to run profiling:
1) New model onboarding
2) Hardware/driver/TF/torch runtime upgrades
3) Before/after kernel updates
4) Regression investigation

Steps (high level):
1) Prepare a sterile test environment: dedicated GPU pool with identical driver and runtime as production canaries.
2) Use the profiling harness (see benchmarking_suite) to run three workloads: microkernels (attention, matmul), end-to-end token generation for typical sequences (short/medium/long), and stress tests at 95th percentile QPS.
3) Collect: GPU traces (nsight/rocprof), runtime traces (OpenTelemetry), memory timelines, temperature, and kernel selection logs.
4) Analyze: compare baseline profiles (stored per-model) against new run. Flag changes if: p50 or p95 regression > 10% or p99 > 5% for critical paths.
5) Post-action: if regression detected, open RFC and follow rollback / kernel pin steps.

Artifacts to produce:
- profile_report.md (summary + graphs)
- raw_trace.{zip} (nsight/rocprof export)
- kernel_selection.log
- config_snapshot.yaml

Best practices:
- Always run at least 3 runs and use the median.
- Use representative prompts from the model's eval prompt-set.
- Record the exact driver/runtime/kernel versions in config_snapshot.yaml.
benchmarking_suite:
Components: a) microbenchmark harness (kernels), b) E2E generation suite, c) multi-tenant stress harness, d) cost/per-token measurement harness.

How to run a canonical benchmark:

1) Checkout repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/serving-benchmarks.git
2) Prepare env: export BENCH_ENV=canary; ./scripts/setup-env.sh --gpu-type a100 --driver 525.85
3) Start collector: ./scripts/start-collector.sh --prom-endpoint http://localhost:9090
4) Run microbench: ./bench run-micro --model gpt-large --shapes "8x512,16x1024" --repeats 5
5) Run e2e: ./bench run-e2e --model gpt-large --prompt_set prompts/short_and_medium.json --max_tokens 512 --repeats 3
6) Run stress: ./bench run-stress --concurrency 500 --qps 200 --duration 900
7) Aggregate: ./bench aggregate --output results/$(date +%F)-gpt-large.json

Key metrics captured:
- tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency per token, GPU utilization, kernel-level occupancy, memory high-water mark, cost-per-token estimate.

Result interpretation:
- A drop in tokens/sec > 10% vs baseline requires an annotated investigation.
- p99 regressions must be investigated immediately; document root cause and mitigation in benchmark report.
release_notes:
Runtime releases follow semantic versioning and ship with migration notes. Recent notable releases:

- v1.5.0 (2025-09-10): Production rollout of adaptive batching, improved kernel probe logic, and per-model kernel pinning. Resolved: p99 regressions on long-context models. Migration: none required, adaptive batching default enabled.
- v1.5.3 (2025-10-12): Hotfix for a memory accounting bug that could undercount KV cache usage (triggered at > 512k tokens cached). Action: upgrade all canaries and dedicated pools.
- v1.6.0-beta (2026-02-14): Introduces continuous kernel benchmarking daemon and automated kernel promotion pipeline. Default disabled; opt-in via feature flag runtime.continuous_kernel_benchmark = true.

Upgrade checklist for operators:
1) Run profiling_playbook before upgrade.
2) Enable feature flags in canary pools only.
3) Monitor p50/p95/p99 and kernel selection logs for 24h.
4) Have rollback plan: revert to previous runtime image and kernel pin config.
known_issues:
Curated list of known issues and mitigations (live update):

- Issue: Intermittent p99 spikes for gpt-xl on sequence lengths > 8k when using quantized kernels.
  Mitigation: Pin to non-quantized kernel for customers with > 1k token contexts; add server-side truncation for free-tier.

- Issue: Underreported GPU memory accounting after multiple model swaps leading to OOMs on long-lived nodes.
  Mitigation: Restart affected worker every 72h; patch v1.5.3 fixes accounting.

- Issue: Kernel probe misclassification after driver upgrade (NVIDIA driver 525.90+).
  Mitigation: Disable auto-probe for that driver until kernel revalidation; node-label affected nodes and exclude from auto-promotion.

- Issue: Excessive batching for low-latency tenants causing latency SLO breaches.
  Mitigation: Per-tenant latency SLA overrides and explicit isolation pool option.
runbooks:
Operational runbooks (short-form) for the most common incidents. For full runbook follow links in team_wiki_and_links.

High-latency p99 incident:
1) Identify affected pool: query latency dashboard, group by pool and model.
2) Check recent kernel selection changes: /var/log/runtime/kernel_selection.log.
3) If kernel change within last 24h, revert to previous kernel via: runtimectl kernel pin --model MODEL --kernel-id KID
4) If batching increase detected, reduce batch_admission_policy to 'conservative' or set max_batch_size lower:
   runtimectl set-config --pool POOL --max_batch_size 8
5) If step 3-4 don't remediate within 15m, migrate traffic to fallback model variant or capacity tier.

OOM on node during model load:
1) Drain node: k8s cordon & drain or cloud provider cordon equivalent.
2) Inspect model artifact size and quantization profile.
3) If model > available memory, reconfigure to quantized variant or move to larger instance type.
4) Restart runtime on node and validate memory accounting.

Kernel probe failure alert:
1) Check probe logs: /opt/runtime/probes/*.log for stack traces.
2) Temporarily disable auto-probe: runtimectl set-config --kernel_probe_enabled false
3) Notify kernel-owners channel and schedule in next maintenance window for deeper investigation.

slos_and_thresholds:
SLOs (example):

- Token-level latency SLO: p50 < 25ms, p95 < 75ms, p99 < 250ms for baseline models on hosted small-capacity pool.
- Availability SLO: 99.95% for dedicated pools (monthly).
- Kernel probe health: no more than 1 failed probe per 24h per node.

Alert thresholds (examples):
- latency_p99_alert: p99 > 300ms for 5m -> page oncall.
- gpu_memory_pressure: node_memory_util_pct > 90% for 2m -> page oncall.
- batch_admission_backlog: queue_length > 500 for 10m -> warn (Slack) and page if persists 30m.
example_commands_and_snippets:
Common admin commands and snippets:

- Check kernel selection for a model: runtimectl kernel status --model gpt-large
- Pin kernel: runtimectl kernel pin --model gpt-large --kernel-id k-20250910-a100
- Check batch queue: runtimectl queue status --pool dedicated-pool-1
- Force garbage collection and restart runtime on node: sudo systemctl stop runtime && sudo rm -f /var/lib/runtime/cache/* && sudo systemctl start runtime
- Run a quick microbenchmark locally: ./bench run-micro --model gpt-medium --shapes "8x512" --repeats 3
